topups.why: Adding hi after the 'pwy bynnag ddudodd …' clause gives 'whoever said …, she was right', which does not hold together; the seed's pattern is 'pwy bynnag … oedd yn iawn'.
In 'oedd o'n anghywir' the o could mean the speaker or the man who isn't ready, so the Welsh and the Korean 그는 are both unclear.
The o in 'oedd o'n anghywir' is unclear and assumes the speaker is male; 'pwy bynnag … oedd yn anghywir' is the natural form.
'o' does not match the plural nhw it seems to point to, and 그는 has no clear referent.

'ddudodd y byddai fo'n anodd' means '(someone) said it would be hard', not 'the person who said'. The Korean does not match, and a Korean version without a subject would allow more than one Welsh answer.
